 SNAP Disagreements Complicate Year-End Farm Bill Talks
 Lawmakers face mounting pressure to reach an agreement before new congressional leadership takes over.
 November 18, 2026 03:00 PM •  
 Neal Burnette-Irwin 
 WASHINGTON, D.C. (RFD-TV) — Congress faces a narrowing window to reach a farm bill agreement before a new congressional class takes office in January.
 Changes to Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits remain a major obstacle. With Democrats set to control the House and Senate Agriculture Committees next year, lawmakers face additional pressure to negotiate before the end of the current session.
 Policy Solutions President Jay Truitt believes an agreement is still possible.
 “Don’t think it’s going to go through regular order, and I know that drives everybody nuts, but I think we’re down to the point where it’s going to end up being like four people in the room, and it’ll be the four people that you like half of them, and you don’t like the other half, no matter who you are, right? They’re going to cut that deal, and again, I think they’ll extend out the reforms on SNAP for a year or two. I do think that E-15 makes the cut.”
 Senate Majority Leader John Thune also highlighted the potential benefits of E15 and permitting reform, including changes intended to reduce regulatory burdens on agricultural producers.
 “This bill will extend Clean Water Act permits for farmers from 5 to 10-years, significantly reducing the frequency with which farmers have to engage with government bureaucracy through that process. This legislation will also provide for faster grazing-related reviews, which will make a real difference to ranchers.”
 Permitting reform cleared a procedural vote last week but continues to face opposition from some Democrats.
 Lawmakers also face a December 11 government funding deadline, with another extension or a combination of funding measures needed to prevent a shutdown.
